verdict.rationale: The SDK documents pausing a run and resuming later from the same RunState, plus built-in session memory and resumable sandbox sessions. A community report also describes a durable Temporal version of the SDK examples, which points to a durable-execution integration path. However, nothing first-party documents surviving process restarts or deploys, or an official durable-execution integration. Missing for 10: first-party docs on RunState serialization and persistence across restarts/deploys, official Temporal or other durable-execution integration docs, hands-on corroboration of crash recovery for long-lived agents.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run long-lived agents durably across process restarts and deploys, natively or via durable-execution integrations

citations.quote: the SDK pauses the run, returns `interruptions`, and lets you resume later from the same `RunState`.
The Agents SDK provides built-in session memory to automatically maintain conversation history across multiple agent runs
Sandbox agents support manifest-defined files, sandbox client selection, and resumable sandbox sessions.
Comparing the durable Temporal version to the original OpenAI Agents SDK examples, it's really not all that different
